summary: Ruriko Sakuma is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at Nagoya University (~1981–1991). She held posts at the Eastern Institute (attested 2015, 2026), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2026), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Rustam Sabirov works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He earned a doctorate in history at Moscow State University by 2004 and has served there as a Senior Researcher.

Ruth Fuller Sasaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Chicago (1927–1929) and under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, Mukai Kono, Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki, and Zuigan Goto. She served as director of the First Zen Institute of America (~1945–1967) and abbess of Ryōsen-an (~1958–1967).

Ruth Gamble is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her Ph.D. at the Australian National University (by 2014) and has held posts as a Research Associate at the Australian National University and as a Post-doctoral Researcher at the University of Munich (attested 2016).
Ryan Anningson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Acadia University and earned his PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University under the supervision of Jason Neelis (attested 2017).

Ryan Matthew Jacobson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a Master of Arts in Religious Studies at Naropa University, where his teachers included Judith Simmer-Brown, D. Phillip Stanley, Sarah Harding, Amelia Hall, Acharya Lama Tenpa Gyaltsen, L. S. Summer, and Jirka Hladis.

Ryan Richard Overbey specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Brown University (AB 2001) and Harvard University (PhD 2010), he has held posts at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, College of the Holy Cross, UC Berkeley (2013–2015), and Wesleyan University (attested 2016).
Ryo Kuroiwa works in computational fields and Indology. He has held appointments at the National Institute of Informatics and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies.
Ryo Nishimura (1972–2016) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Tohoku University from ~1992 to 1996 and under Fumihiko Sueki from ~1996 to 2004.
Ryodo Kudo works in Buddhist studies. He has held teaching posts at Taisho University (attested 2015–2026) and Shukutoku University (attested 2020).

Ryoen Minamoto (1920–2020) specialized in philosophy, Japanology, and religious studies, studying at Kyoto University (~1942–1952). He held posts at Japan Women's University (~1964–1972), Tohoku University (Emeritus Professor ~1984), and International Christian University (~1984–1992).

Ryogon Fukuhara (1909–2000) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1929–1934) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1938–1941). He lectured at Humboldt University (~1939–1941) and served as a professor at Ryukoku University (~1956–1978).
Ryoichi Kondo is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and as president of Tomakomai Komazawa University (attested 2002).

Ryoji Kishino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has served as a part-time lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2026) and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Ryojin Soga (1875–1971) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Otani University, Shinshu University, and under Manshi Kiyozawa. He served as a professor at Toyo University (1916–1924) and held multiple professorships and the presidency (1961–1967) at Otani University.

Ryojun Mitomo is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a professorship at Rissho University Junior College (attested 1996) and served as a professor of social welfare at Rissho University (attested 2001).
Ryoken Nawa works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has served as a commissioned researcher at Kyoto Koka Women's University (attested 2015) and as a lecturer at Osaka University (attested 2026).
Ryoko Mochizuki is an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1963). She served as a lecturer at Rissho University from ~1969 to ~1985.

Ryosaburo Sakaki (1872–1946) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics scholar who studied at Third Higher School and the University of Tokyo (~1892–1895). He lectured at Ryukoku University (1897) and held professorships at Third Higher School (1899) and Kyoto University (1908).

Ryosei Fukuda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University (~1956–1965, PhD 1993). He was appointed professor at Taisho University in 1973 (emeritus 2007) and visiting professor at Shuchiin University in 2012, while also directing institutes including Kawasaki Daishi (attested 2014).
